message.content:
In the repository at /bench/home/work (a Go project called "memos"), I need to determine how caching works.

Investigate and report:
1. Does the project use Redis anywhere for a cache layer? Search for "redis", "Redis", any redis client imports (e.g. go-redis, redigo).
2. How is the cache layer actually implemented? Look for cache-related files/packages (e.g. store/cache, internal cache, LRU, in-memory maps, sync.Map, ristretto, groupcache, etc.). Cite file paths.
3. Is there any TTL applied to user cache entries specifically? Search for user caching and any TTL/expiration configuration. Cite exact file paths and line numbers.

Report concrete findings with file paths and line numbers. If Redis is NOT used, say so explicitly and describe what the actual caching mechanism is.

content.text: I have everything I need. Let me confirm the go.mod has no redis dependency.

Investigation complete. Here are the concrete findings.

## 1. Redis: NOT used anywhere

There is no Redis in this project. A full search for `redis`, `go-redis`, `redigo`, `rueidis` across all `.go`, `go.mod`, and `go.sum` files returned zero results. `go.mod` contains no Redis, ristretto, groupcache, golang-lru, bigcache, freecache, or memcache dependency. Caching is entirely in-process/in-memory.

## 2. Cache implementation: custom in-memory cache built on `sync.Map`

The cache layer is a hand-written, thread-safe, TTL-based in-memory cache.

- **`/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go`** — the implementation.
  - Backed by a `sync.Map` (line 69) with an `atomic.Int64` item counter (line 68).
  - Each entry is an `item` struct holding `value`, `expiration time.Time`, and an approximate `size` (lines 34-39).
  - Defines a `Cache` type plus an `Interface` (lines 11-32) with `Set`, `SetWithTTL`, `Get`, `Delete`, `Clear`, `Size`, `Close`.
  - A background `cleanupLoop` goroutine (lines 200-215) periodically evicts expired items; `Get` also lazily evicts on access (lines 135-144). When `MaxItems` is exceeded, `cleanupOldest` (lines 253-313) drops ~20% of the oldest entries — a rough LRU-by-expiration, not a true LRU library.
- **`/bench/home/work/store/cache.go`** — just a helper `getUserSettingCacheKey` (2-line file).
- **`/bench/home/work/store/store.go`** — wires up three separate cache instances on the `Store` struct (lines 27-29): `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`, all created via `cache.New(cacheConfig)` (lines 51-53) and closed in `Store.Close()` (lines 74-76).

Note: there is a separate, unrelated ad-hoc LRU comment in `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go:377` and another small `instanceStatsCache` used in `server/router/api/v1/instance_stats.go` — but the store-level cache is the one described above.

## 3. TTL on user cache entries: 10 minutes (the default TTL), not a user-specific TTL

There is **no user-specific TTL**. User entries inherit the store-wide default TTL.

- The config that governs the user cache is defined in **`/bench/home/work/store/store.go`, lines 40-45**:
  - `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute` (line 41)
  - `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute` (line 42)
  - `MaxItems: 1000` (line 43)
  - This exact `cacheConfig` is passed to `userCache: cache.New(cacheConfig)` at **line 52**.
- All user writes use the plain `Set` (not `SetWithTTL`), so they get `DefaultTTL`. See **`/bench/home/work/store/user.go`** lines **98, 122, 132, 143, 167**, e.g. `s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user)`.
- `Set` delegates to `SetWithTTL` with the default TTL in **`/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go:93-95`**, and the expiration is stamped at **line 112**: `expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl)`.
- The default of 10 minutes is also duplicated as the package-level default in **`/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go:59`** (`DefaultConfig`), but the store constructs its own config inline rather than calling `DefaultConfig()`.
- User cache invalidation on delete: **`/bench/home/work/store/user_delete.go:39-40`** (`deleteUserCache` → `s.userCache.Delete`).

**Bottom line:** User cache entries expire 10 minutes after they are set (`store.go:41`), enforced by lazy eviction in `Get` (`cache.go:135`) and the 5-minute background `cleanupLoop`. No entry-specific/user-specific TTL override exists anywhere.
